title: Five data-centre linked stocks fall more than 15% as US announces new chip export controls
text:
Five data-centre linked stocks fall more than 15% as US announces new chip export controls Tuesday 17 Nov 2026 BURSA SGX Home 
 Hot Stocks Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 17): Shares of five data centre-linked stocks plunged by as much as 21% on Tuesday, triggering automatic suspensions in intraday short selling (IDSS), as concerns over tighter US export controls on advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips weighed on investor sentiment.
 NationGate Holdings Bhd (KL: NATGATE ), an electronics manufacturing services (EMS) provider and one of Nvidia’s select Asian original equipment manufacturer (OEM) partners, fell to its lowest level since Aug 4 after hitting an intraday low of RM1.32, down 21.43% from its previous close of RM1.68.
 The counter pared some losses to close 23 sen or 13.69% lower at RM1.45, valuing the group at RM3.3 billion.
 Trading volume surged to a near three-month high of 86.47 million shares, making NationGate the fifth most actively traded stock on Bursa Malaysia. The volume was more than three times its 200-day average of 26.62 million shares.
 The sell-off also extended to MN Holdings Bhd (KL: MNHLDG ), Critical Holdings Bhd (KL: CHB ), Pekat Group Bhd (KL: PEKAT ) and Jati Tinggi Group Bhd (KL: JTGROUP ), which are involved in engineering and infrastructure works supporting Malaysia's expanding data centre industry.
 MN Holdings, which specialises in high-voltage power infrastructure, underground utilities engineering and substation construction, fell as much as 69 sen or 20.54% to RM2.67, its lowest level since June 24.
 Similarly, Critical Holdings also dropped as much as 40 sen or 19.51% to RM1.65, its lowest level since July 15.
 Pekat Group meanwhile slid as much as 47 sen or 17.74% to RM2.18, its lowest in nearly two months, while Jati Tinggi fell to a 99-day low of 74 sen, down 15.5 sen or 17.32%. 
 IDSS is automatically triggered when a stock's last traded price falls more than 15 sen or 15% below its reference price. Short selling for all counters will resume at 8.30am on Wednesday.
 The sell-off followed new US export controls tightening China's access to advanced AI chips. The rules require licences for the export, re-export or transfer of advanced semiconductors to Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil, raising concerns over potential disruptions to the chip supply chain.
 The requirements also compel data centres, foreign foundries and chip exporters to conduct enhanced due diligence on customers, including checks on direct or indirect ownership or control by entities in US-embargoed destinations or Macau.
 The broader technology sector also came under pressure, with the Bursa Malaysia Technology Index falling more than 6% on Tuesday.
 An analyst said the new US requirements could delay data centre projects as operators assess the implications of the licensing rules.
 "Notably, the previous AI diffusion rule had delayed data centre project awards by six to seven months.
 "We expect near-term sentiment pressure across power infrastructure names, although contractors with more diversified order books and lower data centre concentration should be relatively less affected," the analyst added.
